text: Duplicate detection was considered and deferred. The user's actual concern is overlapping CSV exports (e.g. a Q1 and a Q2 file sharing rows), not identical real-world transactions. Proposed-but-unbuilt approach: dedupe on (posting date, description, amount, balance) since Chase's Balance column disambiguates two same-day identical purchases. Interim workaround the user accepted: wipe all transactions and reimport. Same acceptance applies to counts_as_spending being computed at import time - changing the spending rule means wipe-and-reimport.

Future intent from the user: (1) import non-Chase bank CSVs - this is why Transaction.raw stores the whole CSV row as JSON regardless of source; (2) flat tags (not hierarchical) assignable to merchants, where a merchant is derived from clean_description - user knows the cleaning is imperfect and wants to refine it with more data before building tagging; (3) the project moved from a single-file Flask script to Django largely because the Django admin gives tag/merchant CRUD for free later. No tag/merchant models exist yet, deliberately.

cdnjs's Chart.js 4.5.0 chart.min.js is the ESM build - it cannot run as a plain script tag (bare-specifier imports, and cdnjs hosts no chunks/ directory, so even type=module fails). The user originally supplied that exact tag with its SRI hash; we verified empirically it cannot work and switched to chart.umd.min.js with its own SRI hash. If anyone swaps the CDN tag back to chart.min.js, both charts break.
